doc.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joe Henderson
summary: Carter recalls writing tunes on the spot for Henderson and praises his playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Let's just play with some more names. A couple of words about … whoever.

Uh … the phantom they used to call Joe. Joe, he never had enough music. And he was always two tunes short, ten minutes, and this is an LP, man, come on Joe. He said, "Hey, big brother, why don't you write me a tune right now?" I said, "Okay." So I wrote Almost 1.5. Power to the People. Did a couple of tunes like that for different projects. Joe had a great mind. I mean, really, really sharp. He didn't talk a whole lot so it's difficult to read him in terms of his emotion for the moment. He played great. It was a pleasure just to hear him play. I'm just sorry that there are not enough guys today who understood Joe's playing or spend enough time listening to want to carry part of Joe's torch in their saxophone.
